analysis:
Examined configuration.md BASE lines 354–709 and the supplied change map/partial patch, including token/state paths, watchdog controls, inference eligibility, memory/media admission, hashing, encrypted SSD and resident cache controls, and environment scrubbing. Most of this surrounding documentation is unchanged; its existing resident-cache language differs from T-041's SSD-only posture, but this PR is not shown to introduce that discrepancy.
The patch adds DARKBLOOM_VERIFIED_WEIGHTS_FILE and describes startup registration reusing owner-only verified hash records bound to file metadata. This changes the weight-identity evidence contract relevant to A-004, T-012, T-027, T-007 and TB-003/TB-007. Owner-only storage alone is not authentication against the adversarial operator. However, neither VerifiedWeightHashStore.swift nor registration/load callers are supplied here, so no exploitable bypass is independently established. Integration must examine record integrity, metadata checks against the actual hashed/loaded files, publication to registration, and whether fresh managed-load verification remains authoritative. BASE configuration.md:578–597 promises full hashing, fresh pre/post-load verification and delayed publication; changed BASE lines 583–584 need reconciliation with the HEAD behavior.
The change map also marks the memory-availability row (BASE:567) and HEAD hashing documentation (584–590), but their complete replacements are absent. Review those changes alongside memory admission and hashing source before concluding security impact. No supplied evidence shows changes to cache salt isolation, AES-GCM/HMAC storage, TTL, attestation authorization, token custody, fan-helper authority, encryption fail-closed behavior or billing. Documentation and bounded excerpts are insufficient to clear the new durable hash-reuse contract.
